title: pvVPICReader
body:
## pvVPICReader

Reads VPIC kinetic plasma particle-in-cell output through its ASCII .vpc file, which describes the per-processor data files, grid size and time steps. Field and hydro quantities are assembled into one uniform image (vtkImageData) of point arrays. Stride subsamples the grid, and XExtent, YExtent and ZExtent restrict which simulation files (the per-processor tiling of the domain) are read, so a subregion can be viewed at full resolution. This is a distributed reader.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Extents count files of the simulation decomposition, not grid cells or physical coordinates.
- Large runs can exceed memory; start with a Stride above 1 or narrower extents.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so check the output on your own files.

Native constructor: `VPICReader`. Identity: `sources/VPICReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FileName` | ASCII .vpc file describes locations of data files, grid sizes, time step sizes and type and order of data written to the files. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `PointArrays` | Variables written to the data files are described in the .vpc file and are presented for selection. Only selected variables are loaded for a time step. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Stride` | VPIC data may be very large and not all is needed for effective visualization. Setting the stride selects every nth data item within the files for display. | `{"items":{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `XExtent` | VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the X dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `YExtent` | VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the Y dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |
| `ZExtent` | VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the Z dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVPICReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
